rooms.body:
# Weiqi LSP Constitution

Audience: the 561 Group board and agents that will materialize, extend, or consume `weiqi-lsp`.

Learning goal: know exactly what `weiqi-lsp` is for, what it may and must refuse, who owns it, and on what authority it exists — before any of its filesystem projections beyond this record and its sibling `SPEC.md` are treated as settled.

## Governance basis

This record uses the same governance basis as its siblings, the [Weiqi Kernel Constitution](./weiqi-kernel-constitution.md) and [Weiqi Platform Constitution](./weiqi-platform-constitution.md), §"Governance basis" — repeated here rather than assumed, since the instruction's named reference (`.agents/skills/corpus-normalization/references/service-section-constitution.md`) still does not exist anywhere in this repository. This record instead draws on `references/repository-model.md`'s own evidence order, the board-approved [Weiqi Platform Plan](./weiqi-platform-plan.md), the board's 2026-08-18 "Board challenge: constituting service sections" note, and the board's 2026-08-11 "standard form" derivation, using both existing sibling records as the "prior constitution record... to serve as a working exemplar" that neither of *them* had when written. As with the kernel and platform, "no speculative scaffolding" means this record lives in the parent's `content/`, not inside a fabricated `services/weiqi-lsp/` or `apps/weiqi-lsp/` directory of its own — admission is not itself an artifact. `SPEC.md`, the rule catalog this record's Board authorization section discusses below, is the one exception this instruction directs explicitly, on the same footing as a constitution record itself: a specification is not the "first real artifact" the plan's scaffolding rule warns against, any more than this document is.

## Distinct responsibility

Machine-verification of every Go-checkable claim this section's own content and app data make — a diagram's stone count, an `expected:` block's recomputed score, a capture/legality assertion, an SGF block's legal replay, a markdown link's resolution, a frontmatter field's presence, a tsumego problem's solvability, a lesson's board-step legality — is one indivisible responsibility that nothing in this repository currently owns in full.

**Founding incident.** On 2026-08-19 — the same day [Regression Positions](./regression-positions.md) was authored — that document's own R9 diagram (the area-score worked example) and its `expected:` block briefly disagreed with each other during authoring: the diagram is the source of truth, and its stone counts, territory counts, and area scores must be *derivable* from it, not merely asserted beside it. The disagreement was caught only because a human re-derived the arithmetic by hand before the position was trusted as a kernel regression fixture — not because any automated process read the diagram, replayed or recomputed it, and checked the `expected:` block's numbers against that computation. No such process existed. `weiqi-kernel`'s own test suite (`apps/weiqi-kernel/test/scoring.test.mts`) now encodes R9 correctly, transcribed by hand a second time by a careful implementer — but the corpus document itself has no standing guarantee that its *next* edit won't reintroduce the same class of slip, silently, since nothing reads `regression-positions.md` and checks it against `weiqi-kernel` the way `weiqi-kernel`'s tests check themselves against it. This is exactly the gap `weiqi-lsp` exists to close, and it is the incident this record's board authorization (below) points to as concrete evidence for what the plan's own regression-corpus clause already anticipated in the abstract.

The nearest existing artifact, `scripts/check-links.mts`, covers only one narrow slice (markdown relative-link resolution) and is not a constituted service — an ungoverned script, absorbed here as one rule family (Family d) rather than left to keep drifting alongside a growing corpus with no owner accountable for the rest of it.

## Generative parent

`weiqi-services-section`, on the same Clause 3.3 grounds as the kernel and platform: `weiqi-lsp` is generated directly from artifacts this section already owns — [Regression Positions](./regression-positions.md)'s diagram-format and `expected:`-block conventions, the corpus's own frontmatter conventions (observed uniformly across its glossary terms, lessons, and notes), and `scripts/check-links.mts`, which this record explicitly absorbs rather than leaves an orphaned side-script. It also reads, read-only, two JSON data files (`tsumego.json`, `lessons.json`) that live under `weiqi-platform`'s own `apps/weiqi-learn/public/data/` — but those files are themselves *extracted* from this section's own `content/text/documents/articles/notes/*.md` sources (each lesson entry in `lessons.json` carries a `_source` pointer back to exactly such a file), so verifying them is still verifying this section's own doctrine, one pipeline stage downstream. That reading relationship is a customer-like consumption of a sibling section's output, on the same footing as `weiqi-platform`'s own read-only consumption of `weiqi-kernel` (see the platform constitution's declared overlap) — never a claim of ownership or generation over `weiqi-platform`'s tree, and never a write into it. `weiqi-services-section` remains the sole generative parent.

## Form: a singular service, not a services-section

Applying the same test as the kernel's and platform's constitutions (2026-08-11 derivation; echoed by the 2026-08-18 board challenge): does the candidate decompose into faces with distinct inputs, outputs, and refusal conditions, or does it collapse to one inseparable operation?

`weiqi-lsp` presents two transport faces — a one-shot CLI (batch-checks a glob of files, exits with a status code) and a long-lived LSP server (streams `didOpen`/`didChange` events over `Content-Length`-framed JSON-RPC, replies with `publishDiagnostics` and `hover`). These differ in transport and cadence, but not in kind: both are thin adapters around one shared verification core that reads a document (from disk or from an in-memory buffer), runs the same rule catalog against it using the same calls into `weiqi-kernel`, and produces the same `Diagnostic` record shape either way. They share one test suite, one rule catalog (`SPEC.md`), one refusal-condition set (never modify a file, never guess a life-and-death verdict, never invent a rule with no cited source), and one customer relationship in the authority sense — an author or a CI process wanting a trustworthy verdict on a document, not two distinct postures the way `weiqi-platform`'s anonymous learner and authenticated player are. This is Clause 1.1's single fiber wearing two thin transport skins, not Clause 2.1's covered region. `weiqi-lsp` is therefore constituted as a **singular service**, matching `weiqi-kernel`'s own form, not a `weiqi-lsp-services-section`.

## Purpose

Machine-verify every claim this section's own content and app data make that a computer can check without guessing: that a hand-drawn ASCII diagram encodes a legal position; that an `expected:` block's stone counts, area/territory scores, and legality claims are exactly what `weiqi-kernel` computes from that same diagram; that any SGF game record embedded in the corpus parses and replays as a legal game; that markdown links and glossary `termRef`s resolve; that frontmatter declares what its content `type` requires; and that the platform's tsumego and lesson app data are internally solvable and legally replayable. `weiqi-lsp` never decides what is *true* about weiqi — `weiqi-kernel` does that — it only checks that what this section *says* agrees with what the kernel *computes*, and reports precisely where it does not.

## Inputs

- Markdown files under this section's own `content/` tree: diagram code fences, `expected:` YAML-ish blocks, relative and site-rooted links, glossary `termRef`-style paths, and frontmatter, per `type` (`term`, `lesson`, `specification`, ...).
- SGF-notation fenced code blocks embedded in that same markdown (a convention this record anticipates rather than one yet exercised by real content — see Open obligations).
- Two read-only JSON data files owned by `weiqi-platform`'s Learn face: `tsumego.json` (problems, accepted moves, reply lines) and `lessons.json` (steps, worked board positions, sequences).
- `weiqi-kernel`'s exported functions (`Game`, `findGroup`, `coordToPoint`, `scoreArea`/`scoreTerritory`, `sgfToGameRecord`, the semantic event layer), consumed as a pure library dependency and never reimplemented.
- For the LSP face specifically: `initialize`, `didOpen`, `didChange`, `didClose`, and `hover` requests over `Content-Length`-framed JSON-RPC on stdio.

## Outputs

- A list of typed `Diagnostic` records — `code` (a `WQ0xx` identifier from `SPEC.md`'s catalog), `severity`, `file`, `location`, a human-readable `message`, and the normative source document the violated rule enforces — produced identically by both transport faces.
- For the CLI face: a process exit code (0/1/2, see `SPEC.md`) plus either human-readable text or, under `--json`, the diagnostics array as machine-readable output on stdout.
- For the LSP face: `publishDiagnostics` notifications per open document, and `hover` responses over a diagram coordinate reporting kernel-mechanical facts only (group membership, liberty count, occupancy) — never a life-and-death verdict.
- `weiqi-lsp` produces no other artifact. It never writes, moves, renames, or reformats any file it checks, under any invocation or flag.

## Customers

Content authors, human and agent, editing this section's markdown and app data (the LSP face, live in an editor, and the CLI face, run by hand before a commit); CI, as an automated gate run against every change to this section's content or the platform's app data; and the editor itself, as the LSP client process that speaks the protocol on an author's behalf. `weiqi-lsp` has no end-user-facing customer at all — like `weiqi-kernel`, it is infrastructure for the people and processes that produce and guard this section's doctrine, never something a learner or player interacts with directly.

## Authority

- **Closed-world signature (2026-08-11 derivation, Clause 3.2):** `weiqi-lsp` may be invoked only through its declared CLI entry point and its declared LSP JSON-RPC methods (`initialize`, `didOpen`, `didChange`, `didClose`, `hover`, plus the diagnostics-publishing direction). No caller may reach into its rule implementations to bypass a check or force a diagnostic to disappear; there is no other door, and there is no `--fix`.
- **Stratum:** the same `apps/<domain>-computer` purity tier as `weiqi-kernel`, per the 2026-08-11 derivation's product-spine Clause 5 — no network socket, no credential, no clock it was not handed. The LSP face's stdio JSON-RPC framing is a process-local pipe, not a network listener, so it does not cross into the `services/<domain>-server` tier the way `weiqi-platform`'s future Play face will.
- **Change authority:** `weiqi-lsp`'s rule catalog is strictly downstream of the documents each rule cites — `regression-positions.md`'s diagram format, this corpus's own frontmatter conventions, `check-links.mts`'s absorbed logic, and the app-data schemas `tsumego.json`/`lessons.json` already use. A change to what counts as valid is authored in one of those places first; it is never invented ad hoc inside the checker. And for anything `weiqi-kernel` can already compute — legality, scoring, group/liberty facts — `weiqi-lsp` never reimplements the computation locally; it always calls the kernel and reports disagreement, on exactly the restriction `weiqi-platform`'s own constitution places on its Learn and Play faces ("any move validation not delegated to `weiqi-kernel` is a refusal-worthy violation").
- **Runtime authority:** none beyond what any pure, read-only tool has. It holds no credentials, opens no socket, and persists no state across invocations — an LSP session's per-document diagnostics live only in server memory for that session's lifetime, never written to disk.

## Non-ownership

`weiqi-lsp` does not own: corpus content (authorship of lessons, glossary terms, notes, and their diagrams remains the human or agent author's own act — `weiqi-lsp` reports, it never drafts or corrects); rules computation of any kind (legality, scoring, ko/superko, SGF semantics, semantic-event recognition — all `weiqi-kernel`'s, consumed read-only, per the closed-world signature above); app-data authorship (`tsumego.json` and `lessons.json` remain `weiqi-platform`'s own generated/authored artifacts, read by `weiqi-lsp` but never written); and CI policy (whether a given diagnostic code blocks a merge, and at what severity threshold, is CI's own configuration downstream of this tool's exit code — not a decision `weiqi-lsp` makes about its own output).

Stated as its own clause because it is the single most important boundary this record draws: **`weiqi-lsp` never modifies files.** Under no flag, no invocation mode, no diagnostic severity does it write to, rename, reformat, or delete anything it checks. It verifies content; it never generates or owns it. Adding an auto-fix capability of any kind would require a new constitution, not an amendment to this one — "verify, never author" is definitional to why this service exists apart from the content it checks.

## Refusal conditions

`weiqi-lsp` must refuse (report an explicit, honestly-scoped diagnostic, never a silent best-effort guess) when:

- an `expected:` block asserts a claim that requires life-and-death reading beyond what `weiqi-kernel` can mechanically decide — a `status: seki` or `status: dead` claim (regression positions R6, R7) is reported as **not verified**, with the mechanical facts the checker *did* confirm (liberties, group membership) stated alongside, never silently passed as though the status word itself had been confirmed and never contradicted by a guess. This mirrors `weiqi-kernel`'s own events-layer doctrine exactly: `cut`, `false-eye`, `seki`, and `group-settled` are deliberately undetected there for the identical reason, and `weiqi-lsp` inherits that boundary rather than working around it;
- a regression position's own prose disclaims a literal move trace — R2 and R3's `note:` fields state outright that they are "structural specification[s], not fully traced sequence[s]" — in which case legality-replay verification (Family b) is skipped for that position by id, with an explicit diagnostic saying so, rather than fabricating an intervening move list to satisfy the rule;
- its own precondition cannot be evaluated at all — the `weiqi-kernel` import fails, a glob matches zero files, a JSON data file does not parse, or an SGF block cannot even be tokenized — in which case the run reports a tool-level failure (exit code 2, or an explicit diagnostic of its own), never a silent pass;
- asked, by any flag or protocol request, to modify, reformat, or auto-correct a file — there is no such capability to invoke, per Non-ownership above;
- asked to check a claim against a rule with no citable normative source — every rule in `SPEC.md`'s catalog names the convention document it enforces; a proposed rule with nothing to cite is refused until a source exists, per this house's ethos that the checker's rules *are* doctrine enforcement, not free-floating lint preference.

`weiqi-lsp` must never silently degrade a check, guess at a caller's intent on malformed input, or produce a diagnostic (or its absence) it cannot justify against a normative source document or a `weiqi-kernel` computation.

## Board authorization

The 561 Group board approved the [Weiqi Platform Plan](./weiqi-platform-plan.md) on 2026-08-18. That plan itself states the textual warrant this record acts on directly: "Property-based tests (round-trip SGF, ko/superko invariants, scoring cross-checks against known positions), plus a corpus of regression positions drawn from the rules-completeness documents so the doctrine and the code cite each other." `weiqi-lsp` is the machine that keeps that citation honest on an ongoing basis, not just at the moment a regression position is first hand-verified — and the 2026-08-19 R9 incident cited under Distinct responsibility above is concrete, dated evidence of exactly the failure mode that clause was written to prevent.

That said, the plan's own "Board decisions requested" item 1 — "Approve platform placement inside `weiqi-services-section` and the two child-section constitutions (kernel, platform app)" — named only two children by number. `weiqi-lsp` is a third, admitted by neither that vote nor any later one. This record therefore does what the kernel's and platform's own records do when a question is not settled by their evidence: it states the tension rather than presuming past it. This record authorizes only the *constitution* of `weiqi-lsp` — its existence, boundary, and authority as argued above — and it explicitly requests the board's ratification of this third admission at its next opportunity, per the board challenge note's acceptance test 4 ("refuse materialization without explicit authority"). It does not, by itself, authorize materialization of any `src/`, `test/`, `package.json`, or protocol implementation beyond the one artifact this same instruction separately directs: the rule-catalog specification, `apps/weiqi-lsp/SPEC.md`, which — like this constitution itself — is not the "first real artifact" the plan's no-speculative-scaffolding clause warns against, but the reviewable act of admission that must exist *before* it.

## Open obligations

- **Ratification of a third child admission**, per Board authorization above: this record makes the case; it does not itself constitute board approval of a vote that has not yet occurred.
- **SGF rule family ships ahead of any content that exercises it.** No `.md` file in this section's corpus currently contains a fenced SGF block; Family (c)'s rules are specified in `SPEC.md` against the day one appears, tested only against synthetic fixtures until then — the same "no speculative scaffolding" posture applied at the rule level, not only the directory level.
- **Cross-section site-rooted paths remain out of scope.** Frontmatter `requires:`/`uses-mechanic:` entries rooted at `/games/...` outside this section's own `/games/topics/board-games/weiqi/...` prefix belong to a site-wide URL namespace this section does not own or control the filesystem shape of (the same reason `check-links.mts` already skips all `/`-rooted paths); `weiqi-lsp` resolves only the sub-prefix mounted onto this section's own tree and explicitly does not attempt to verify the rest. This is a documented scope boundary, not a defect, unless and until a sibling section constitutes an equivalent checker of its own.
- **Naming**, echoing the kernel's and platform's own flagged tensions rather than resolving one here: this instruction's given name and address, `weiqi-lsp` at `apps/weiqi-lsp`, names the tool after one of its two transport faces (the LSP surface) even though its distinct responsibility, per this record, is closer to "content checker" than "language server" — `SPEC.md`'s CLI face is not a lesser or secondary interface, both are load-bearing. Carried forward as an open naming note, not resolved by fiat, consistent with how the kernel and platform records both handle their own open naming questions.

## What comes next

`apps/weiqi-lsp/SPEC.md` — the rule catalog, CLI contract, and LSP surface this constitution authorizes the specification of — is the next act this service owes itself before any `src/`, `test/`, or `package.json` may appear under its own materialization address. See the sibling [Weiqi Kernel Constitution](./weiqi-kernel-constitution.md) for the pure computation `weiqi-lsp` calls and never reimplements, and the [Weiqi Platform Constitution](./weiqi-platform-constitution.md) for the section whose Learn-face app data this service reads, read-only, as one of its verification targets.

rooms.description: Competitive teardown of 2025-2026 mobile and browser Go apps (BadukPop, GoMagic, Tsumego Pro, OGS, Fox/Yike, AI Sensei, EasyGo, PlayGo.gg) with a feature-parity checklist for the browser-first weiqi platform. Audience: the 561 Group board and implementing agents.
rooms.body:
# Weiqi Market Teardown

Research provenance: compiled 2026-08-19 by a web-research agent; sourced with URLs inline. Companion to the Weiqi Platform Plan — this document is the Phase 2 (parity) feature spec's evidence base.

## Headline findings

1. **The differentiator is validated open territory.** No incumbent — including PlayGo.gg, the ambitious chess.com-for-Go entrant launched February 2026 — links live gameplay to contextual concept teaching. Every glossary found (Sensei's Library, GoMagic's term pages, PlayGo.gg's terms page) is a static reference the player must leave the board to consult. Glossary-linked play (the kernel recognizes atari/ko/seki as they occur and surfaces the definition in place) is claimed by nobody.
2. **The most repeated complaint across the market is "right/wrong, no why"** — tsumego apps mark answers without explaining the concept. The semantic-event layer answers this complaint by construction.
3. **Fragmentation is the opening.** OGS is play-only (AI review paywalled), GoMagic is curriculum-only (play "coming soon"), AI Sensei is analysis-only, Tsumego Pro is puzzles-only. Nobody unifies play + graded curriculum + contextual explanation + review in one browser product.
4. **Two features are near-unclaimed:** spaced repetition (only EasyGo, a niche power-user app) and personalized problems generated from your own game mistakes (only AI Sensei).
5. **OGS's mobile ergonomics are the incumbent browser weakness to not repeat:** confirm/pass button below the fold causing misclicks, no zoom/precision placement aid, no onboarding skill assessment.

## App-by-app profiles

### BadukPop (CorePlane Inc. — iOS/Android)
- **Play**: automatch online, correspondence, 9x9/13x13/19x19, spectating. **Bots**: personality AIs, 20 kyu to 7+ dan. **Tsumego**: 4,000–5,000+ pro-curated; rated + practice modes; dailies. **Lessons**: interactive, rules through tesuji. **Review**: auto AI scoring only. **Monetization**: Pro $6.99 one-time or $49.99/yr; coin packs $0.99–$39.99.
- **Complaints**: puzzle explanations don't say *why*; AI sometimes appears to violate rules it just taught; matchmaking mismatches; narrow tsumego variety (liberty-shortage-heavy).
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/badukpop-go/id1472684271) · [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.coreplane.badukpop.prod&hl=en_CA) · [negative reviews](https://appgrooves.com/app/badukpop-go-weiqi-game-by-badukpop-go-coreplane-inc/negative)

### GoMagic (gomagic.org — web + Android TWA)
- **Play**: none — "coming soon." **Tsumego**: 5,877-puzzle Skill Tree, coin gamification, daily free problem. **Lessons**: 29 interactive courses, 278 videos (~50h), rank-banded (25–15k / 12–2k / 5k–5d) — the strongest curriculum in the field. **Review**: upcoming, not shipped. **Monetization**: subs $9.90–$33.30/mo + à la carte courses $19.90–$149.90. **Glossary**: static term pages only.
- [GoMagic](https://gomagic.org/) · [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.gomagic.twa&hl=en_US) · [Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/gomagic.org)

### Tsumego Pro (LR Studios — iOS/Android)
- **Pure problems app**: 6 free daily problems, adaptive Progress mode, offline packs (a real differentiator), hints, all-valid-answer display. **No explanations** — the persistent multi-year complaint: right/wrong but never *why* (no seki/ko/life explanation); accepts only one of several valid solutions; beginner-hostile terminology.
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tsumego-pro-go-problems/id892041876) · [negative reviews](https://appgrooves.com/app/tsumego-pro-go-problems-by-emmanuel-mathis/negative?load_all=1)

### OGS — online-go.com (the browser incumbent)
- **Play**: live/blitz/correspondence, all board sizes, multiple rulesets, tournaments, ladders, groups. **Bots**: ~30 graded. **Puzzles**: community-submitted, uneven curation. **Lessons**: none in-house. **Review**: KataGo AI review paywalled behind Supporter (~$10/mo historically). **Rating**: Glicko-2, respected. **Mobile**: responsive web only; PWA installability unconfirmed.
- **Complaints (the "what to beat" list)**: misclicks on phones — confirm button below the fold forces scrolling that re-selects intersections ([thread](https://forums.online-go.com/t/misclick-on-phone/30202), [thread](https://forums.online-go.com/t/problems-using-ogs-on-mobile/49128)); no zoom aid for precise placement; no onboarding skill assessment ([thread](https://forums.online-go.com/t/new-player-ogs-user-experience/38482)); confusing layout for newcomers; free tier gets weak/no AI review.
- [Support](https://online-go.com/support) · [Supporter](https://online-go.com/supporter) · [Glicko-2](https://forums.online-go.com/t/ogs-has-a-new-glicko-2-based-rating-system-2017/13058) · [goratings](https://github.com/online-go/goratings/blob/master/RatingsV6.md)

### Fox Weiqi / Yike Weiqi (China-centric incumbents)
- **Play**: 40,000+ concurrent claimed (pros included), live pro tournaments with human+AI commentary. **Unique**: photo-to-digitized-record analysis (camera at physical board) — no Western competitor has it. **Tsumego**: tens of thousands. **But**: China-region-locked in practice; heavy aggressive ads (auto-redirects, unskippable, even for paying members); iOS stability complaints.
- [Fox International](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.foxwq.yhwqgl&hl=en_US) · [Yike](https://apps.apple.com/app/id988682022)

### AI Sensei (browser analysis service)
- **Core**: upload/import SGF → KataGo review, mistake navigation, quiz mode; **turns your own mistakes into custom practice problems** (distinctive). **Tiers by KataGo depth**: Free (10 playouts) → Basic $5.95 → Dan $11.95 → Pro $27.95/mo. **Bots**: humanlike 30k–9d. **PWA-installable** — the one incumbent doing installable-web adequately. No curriculum, no ladder.
- [AI Sensei](https://ai-sensei.com/) · [FAQ](https://ai-sensei.com/faq)

### KataGo-trainer tier (KaTrain, EasyGo, AI KataGo Tsumego)
- **KaTrain** (desktop): weakened/styled KataGo bots, costliest-mistake review with retry — the reference UX for "AI that teaches while it plays." [GitHub](https://github.com/sanderland/katrain)
- **EasyGo** (mobile): **on-device offline KataGo**, calibrated human-style ranks, 2,400+ problems, **real spaced repetition** (Fail/Hard/Easy scheduling) — the clearest SRS in any Go app. [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.jiaxiang.easygo)
- **AI KataGo Go: Tsumego**: 27,000+ problems. [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.navibarda.katago&hl=en_US)

### PlayGo.gg (launched Feb 2026 — the competitor to watch)
- Chess.com-for-Go positioning: fast matchmaking, Puzzle Run (20,000+ puzzles, boss puzzles), AI review + coaching, pro lessons, weekly cash-prize pro tournaments, rewards store; human-move heatmaps ("what would a human play here") — novel and worth matching. Static glossary with lesson links but **no live in-game concept recognition**. Experimenting with luck-based mechanics (randomized starts, powerups) that risk alienating traditional players. Web + Google Play; multilingual.
- [PlayGo.gg](https://www.playgo.gg/) · [AGA launch coverage](https://www.usgo.org/content.aspx?page_id=5&club_id=454497&item_id=131609) · [glossary](https://www.playgo.gg/learn/terms)

### Also noted
- **GoQuest**: fast 9x9/13x13 matchmaking; complaints: unskippable audio ads, fixed komi/time presets. [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/goquest/id834841918)
- **Omoyo**: AI personalities, live winrate graph, "intelligent solver" that *responds* to wrong tsumego answers in real time rather than showing the solution — a UX idea worth studying. [Omoyo](https://omoyo.app/)
- **Sensei's Library**: 26,000+ page wiki, zero play integration — confirming the open differentiator. [senseis.xmp.net](https://senseis.xmp.net/)

## Feature-parity checklist

Legend: ✅ has it · ➖ partial/weak · ❌ absent · — n/a

| Feature | BadukPop | GoMagic | Tsumego Pro | OGS | Fox/Yike | AI Sensei | EasyGo | PlayGo.gg | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Live online play (matchmaking) | ✅ | ❌ | — | ✅ | ✅ | ➖ | ➖ | ✅ | **MUST-HAVE** |
| Async/correspondence play | ✅ | ❌ | — | ✅ | ➖ | ❌ | ❌ | ➖ | MUST-HAVE |
| AI bots, graded strength range | ✅ | ❌ | — | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | MUST-HAVE |
| Curated graded tsumego library | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ➖ | ✅ | ➖ | ✅ | ✅ | MUST-HAVE |
| Structured lessons/courses | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ➖ | ❌ | ➖ | ✅ | MUST-HAVE |
| AI post-game review | ➖ | ❌ | — | ✅(paywalled) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | MUST-HAVE |
| Personalized problems from own mistakes | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ➖ | **DIFFERENTIATOR** |
| Spaced repetition (SRS) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | **DIFFERENTIATOR** |
| Streaks/dailies/gamified rewards | ➖ | ➖ | ➖ | ❌ | ➖ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | DIFFERENTIATOR |
| Rank/rating system | ✅ | ➖ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | MUST-HAVE |
| Glossary / terminology reference | ❌ | ✅(static) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅(static) | MUST-HAVE (baseline) |
| **Live in-game concept recognition + contextual surfacing** | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | **THE DIFFERENTIATOR — nobody has this** |
| Offline play/study | ➖ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | DIFFERENTIATOR |
| PWA / installable web app | ❌ | ➖ | — | ➖ | ❌ | ✅ | — | ➖ | MUST-HAVE |
| Photo/OCR of physical board | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | SKIP (niche for browser-first education product) |
| Tournaments/ladders | ➖ | ❌ | — | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | — | ✅ | DIFFERENTIATOR |
| Ad-supported free tier | ➖ | ❌ | ➖ | ➖ | ✅(heavy) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | SKIP — ads are a top complaint everywhere |
| Multi-language / i18n | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | ➖ | ➖ | ➖ | ✅ | MUST-HAVE |
| Human coaching/teacher access | ❌ | ➖ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | DIFFERENTIATOR |
| Human-move heatmap (vs pure winrate) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | DIFFERENTIATOR — worth matching |

## Incumbent weaknesses (evidenced)

1. **"Right/wrong, no why"** — the single most repeated complaint (BadukPop, Tsumego Pro, and by omission everywhere). A glossary-linked engine names the concept (seki, ko threat, false eye) *at the moment of the mistake*.
2. **Mobile touch ergonomics** — OGS's below-the-fold confirm button causes misclicks; no zoom/precision aid. Browser UX debt a new platform must simply not repeat.
3. **Matchmaking/rating mismatch frustration** (BadukPop); fixed komi/time presets (GoQuest).
4. **Ads as friction** — Fox/Yike's auto-redirecting unskippable ads even for payers; GoQuest's audio ads. Avoid importing this complaint pattern.
5. **Play/learn/analyze fragmentation** — the biggest structural opening; nobody unifies all three.
6. **Paywalling exactly what helps you improve** — OGS/AI Sensei/GoMagic all gate the teaching. Free always-on contextual teaching (concept recognition, not deep KataGo search) sidesteps this resentment even if deep review is paid.
7. **China lock-out** — Fox/Yike are inaccessible/unreliable outside China, leaving the "best mainstream Go app" seat only partially filled in the West.
8. **No SRS almost anywhere** — well-understood Duolingo/Anki-style mechanics, essentially unclaimed.

## What "beat them in-browser" concretely requires

**Performance targets**: FCP < 1.8s, Speed Index < 3.4s as floor ([PWA guide](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/progressive-web-apps-2026-pwa-performance-guide)); sub-100ms input-to-paint on stone placement (the interaction repeated hundreds of times per session); full Lighthouse Installable + PWA-Optimized pass (HTTPS, manifest, service worker) — table stakes that most of the field fails, so passing is itself differentiating.

**Mobile-web UX**: persistent thumb-reachable action bar (never below-the-fold confirm); magnifier-on-touch / snap-to-nearest-intersection placement preview; onboarding skill assessment; offline-cached study content (tsumego, lessons, glossary) even though live play needs connectivity.

**What native still genuinely wins (architect around, don't deny)**: reliable background push (iOS web push requires home-screen install, still less reliable — correspondence "your turn" notifications will lag native); background compute (run KataGo review server-side with completion notification, never client-background); on-device offline AI at strength (offer a weaker WASM offline bot honestly rather than promising full-strength offline); OS deep integration (camera board digitization, widgets, haptics); app-store discovery (substitute SEO + streamer/pro partnerships, as PlayGo.gg does).

## Net positioning

The differentiator is confirmed open: recognize concepts live on the board and teach in place, free and always-on. But it only wins if the table stakes are also cleared — live play, graded bots, curated tsumego, Glicko-2 ratings, real PWA installability, and mobile touch ergonomics that fix what OGS visibly broke. The unclaimed adjacencies worth taking early: spaced repetition over the concept graph (the ontology already models it) and personalized problems from the player's own semantic-event history (our kernel emits exactly the evidence needed).

rooms.body:
Audience: readers who want a first structural map of weiqi before studying joseki, life and death, or advanced strategy.

Learning goal: explain how liberties, capture, territory, and ko organize play in weiqi.

## Worked example: surrounding one stone

Imagine an empty 9 by 9 board. Black places one stone near the center. White then places stones on each of the four adjacent intersections around it. Once Black's stone has no remaining [liberties](../../../glossary/terms/liberty.md), White removes it from the board. That is a [capture](../../../glossary/terms/capture.md).

This small example shows the core logic of the game. Stones do not move after placement. They remain in place, connect to neighboring stones of the same color, and survive only while the group retains at least one liberty. Much of weiqi can be understood as managing that relation between extension and enclosure.

Weiqi is a two-player territorial board game played by placing black and white stones on grid intersections, usually on a 19 by 19 board [@britannica2026go; @nagofed2026thisisgo]. Black moves first. Stones normally remain where they are played unless they are captured. Because the board state is almost fully public, the game rewards long-range spatial judgment rather than hidden-information inference.

The central tactical unit is the liberty. A single stone in open space has four liberties, fewer on the edge, and fewer again in the corner. Connected stones share liberties, which is why groups matter more than isolated stones. When a move removes the last liberty from an opposing stone or group, the player captures it and removes it from the board [@nagofed2026thisisgo]. A stone or group reduced to one liberty is in [atari](../../../glossary/terms/atari.md), which is the game's simplest tactical alarm.

The strategic objective is [territory](../../../glossary/terms/territory.md), not only capture. Players try to secure vacant points by surrounding them more solidly than the opponent can invade or reduce [@britannica2026go; @nagofed2026thisisgo]. This is why a move that does not capture anything immediately can still be strong: it may stabilize a large territorial framework or prevent the opponent from doing so.

The game also needs a rule to prevent immediate infinite repetition. That rule is [ko](../../../glossary/terms/ko.md): after a capture that would allow the opponent to recreate the exact previous board position with one move, that immediate recapture is forbidden [@britgo2025default]. Ko turns some local fights into timing problems that reach across the whole board, because the player who is blocked from recapturing must play elsewhere first.

## Exercises

1. Why is a group of connected stones usually stronger than the same number of isolated stones?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

Connected stones share liberties. That usually makes them harder to capture because the opponent must remove the liberties of the whole group, not each stone separately.
</details>

2. Why is ko important even though it applies only to a narrow kind of local repetition?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

Without ko, some local captures could repeat forever and stop the game from progressing. Ko forces the fight to break and often links a local struggle to the wider board because one player must play elsewhere first.
</details>

## What comes next

The next step is [Living Groups and Eyes](./living-groups-and-eyes.md), which explains why [connection](../../../glossary/terms/connection.md) and [eyes](../../../glossary/terms/eye.md) determine whether groups survive. For scoring and matchmaking structure, continue with [Komi and Handicap](./komi-and-handicap.md). For vocabulary work, continue with [Terms](../../../glossary/topics/weiqi.md), especially [liberty](../../../glossary/terms/liberty.md), [atari](../../../glossary/terms/atari.md), [eye](../../../glossary/terms/eye.md), and [life and death](../../../glossary/terms/life-and-death.md).

rooms.body:
# Weiqi Platform Constitution

Audience: the 561 Group board and agents that will materialize, extend, or consume `weiqi-platform`.

Learning goal: know exactly what `weiqi-platform` covers, which faces it admits now versus later, who owns each, and what it may and must refuse — before any of its filesystem projections are treated as settled.

## Governance basis

This record uses the same governance basis as its sibling [Weiqi Kernel Constitution](./weiqi-kernel-constitution.md), §"Governance basis" — repeated here rather than assumed: the instruction's named reference, `.agents/skills/corpus-normalization/references/service-section-constitution.md`, does not exist anywhere in this repository, and no prior constitution record exists as a working exemplar. This record instead draws on `references/repository-model.md`'s own evidence order, the board-approved [Weiqi Platform Plan](./weiqi-platform-plan.md), the board's 2026-08-18 "Board challenge: constituting service sections" note, and the board's 2026-08-11 "standard form" derivation — in particular its Clause 2 definition of a *services-section* as a region of the base with a covering (a declared set of member services), mandatory overlap declarations even when the cover is currently discrete, and Clause 3.3's rule that containment must match generation.

As with the kernel, the plan's "no speculative scaffolding" clause means this record lives in the parent's `content/`, not inside a fabricated `services/weiqi-platform/` directory — admission is not itself an artifact.

## Distinct responsibility

Serving weiqi as a product — teaching it and, later, hosting play of it — over one shared concept graph is a responsibility no existing service in this repository owns. `weiqi-services-section` currently owns corpus content and (via its sibling constitution) will own the pure rules kernel; neither owns rendering, interactivity, deployment, accounts, or real-time play. The plan's central differentiator — glossary-linked play, where the interface surfaces the corpus's own term and lesson content at the moment a recognized event occurs on the board — requires a component that sits between the kernel's semantic events and a human reader, choosing what to render and when. Nothing upstream of this admission does that, and it cannot be folded into the kernel (which must stay pure, per its own constitution) or into raw content (which is prose, not an interactive surface).

## Generative parent

`weiqi-services-section`, on the same Clause 3.3 grounds as the kernel: the platform is generated directly from this section's corpus (the lesson template it interactively ports, the seventeen glossary terms it renders as hover-cards, the ontology it consumes as a skill tree) and from the kernel this section also constitutes. No other section generates it.

## Form: a services-section, not a singular service

Applying the same test as the kernel's constitution (2026-08-11 derivation; echoed by the 2026-08-18 board challenge): does the candidate decompose into faces with distinct inputs, outputs, and refusal conditions, or does it collapse to one inseparable operation?

The plan's own description of `weiqi-platform` names two faces with genuinely different natures, not two implementation details of one operation:

1. **The Learn face** (Phase 1, admitted now) — board component, interactive lessons, tsumego player, glossary pages. Client-side and static assets only. Per the plan verbatim: "no accounts, no server state, deployable exactly like 561.group." Its refusal condition is structural: it must hold no network key, no socket, and no persistent write path — it is the `apps/<domain>-computer` purity tier of the 2026-08-11 derivation's product spine, applied to this domain.
2. **The Play face** (Phase 2+, declared but not yet admitted) — the Durable-Object game-room service: WebSocket hub, authoritative clock, D1-backed accounts and game archive. Its refusal condition is the mirror image: it is exactly where, per the same derivation, "keys and sockets enter," and it must refuse to let any client bypass the kernel's own move validation.

These two faces have distinct inputs (a lesson/tsumego selection vs. a move over a live socket), distinct outputs (rendered instructional state vs. an authoritative game-state broadcast), distinct customers in the authority sense (an anonymous learner needing no account vs. an authenticated player in a stateful room), and distinct refusal conditions (a purity boundary that runs in opposite directions). This is precisely Clause 2.1's covered region, not Clause 1.1's single fiber. `weiqi-platform` is therefore constituted as a **services-section**, `weiqi-platform-services-section`, with the cover declared below.

**Open naming tension, not resolved here**, on the same grounds as the kernel's: this repository's convention names services-sections with a `-services-section` suffix; the plan and this instruction's given path use the bare `weiqi-platform`. Carried forward as an open obligation.

## Cover, overlaps, and stratum (2026-08-11 derivation, Clause 2.1/2.2/§6)

A section's export is its incidence data, not a bag of entries. Declared now, ahead of any materialization:

- **Cover** (intended, not all yet admitted):
  - `weiqi-platform-learn-service` — the Phase 1 static education app. Admitted by this record as the section's first member once its own constitution record is written (this document constitutes the *section*; the Learn service's own constitution, satisfying the same field list, is a follow-on act this section owes before that child directory may appear — see Open obligations).
  - `weiqi-platform-play-service` — the Phase 2+ Durable-Object play service. Declared, not admitted: no constitution record exists for it yet, and none should until Phase 1 ships and the board authorizes Phase 2, per the plan's roadmap and the challenge note's acceptance test 4.
- **Overlaps** (mandatory to declare even before both members exist, per Clause 2.2 — an undeclared cover is not license to skip this, it is the reason to state the *intended* overlap now so it is not silently invented later):
  - `weiqi-platform-learn-service | weiqi-platform-play-service`: shared carrier = the board rendering component, the glossary hover-card component, and the `weiqi-kernel` dependency itself (both faces validate and render moves through the same kernel; the plan states this outright — "a capture in a live game, an exercise in a lesson, and the glossary entry for 'capture' are the same node seen three ways"). Until the play service exists, this overlap is **declared-discrete** — stated as an intended, not yet checkable, agreement — rather than presented as proven coherence.
- **Restrictions:** the Learn service must restrict to the overlap by treating the kernel and shared components as read-only dependencies (it introduces no new event vocabulary of its own). The Play service, once admitted, must restrict to the same overlap identically — no divergent board-rendering or event-naming logic is permitted to develop in either face independently of the other.
- **Stratum:** L3 (computing/services) for the section as a whole, per the ontological-spine tower — it is the tier where the kernel's L2 rule structure meets an actual client or server. The Learn face sits at the `apps/<domain>-computer` purity sub-tier (no keys); the Play face, once admitted, sits at the `services/<domain>-server` sub-tier (keys and sockets enter). Neither face may import downward past the kernel's L2 boundary in a way that reimplements rules logic.

## Purpose

Serve weiqi as one product across three faces built from one concept graph — Play, Learn, and Read (the living glossary/library, served as pages and an API) — with education as the organizing principle: the Learn face ships complete and usable on its own before any multiplayer complexity is admitted. The platform's differentiator is glossary-linked play: surfacing this section's own term and lesson definitions at the moment the kernel's semantic events make them relevant.

## Inputs

- **Learn face:** a learner's navigation/selection (which lesson, which tsumego, which glossary term), rendered client-side against the corpus and the kernel's pure computation. No account, no server round-trip.
- **Play face (future):** authenticated player actions over a WebSocket connection to a Durable Object game room; clock state; reconnection requests.
- Both faces: the kernel's position/legality/scoring/event outputs (consumed, never reimplemented) and this section's own corpus content (lessons, glossary, ontology) as the source of every rendered explanation.

## Outputs

- **Learn face:** rendered board state, step-through worked examples, playable tsumego with revealed commentary on request, glossary hover-cards, and a learner's local progress against the concept graph.
- **Play face (future):** authoritative game-state broadcasts to players and spectators, SGF export, a post-game concept-event timeline, and persisted game/rating records.
- Both: every rendered move or lesson event links to its glossary term page, per the shared hover-card component declared in the overlap above.

## Customers

End users in two distinct postures, matching the cover: an anonymous or lightly-identified learner (Learn face — the plan's explicit Phase 1 target, "no account required" for the first session) and an authenticated player, teacher, or spectator (Play face, once admitted). Internally, both faces are customers of `weiqi-kernel` and of `weiqi-services-section`'s own corpus content — this section produces no rules content and no corpus content of its own; it renders and serves what its generative parent and sibling already define.

## Authority

- **Closed-world signature:** each admitted member of the cover may only invoke the operators it declares. The Learn face's declared signature holds no network or key operator at all (the purity boundary is not a preference, it is the boundary that makes Phase 1 deployable exactly like 561.group with zero operational burden). The Play face, once admitted, is the only place in this whole section where keys, sockets, and a clock the process was not handed are permitted to enter, per the 2026-08-11 derivation's Clause 5.
- **Change authority:** UI, deployment, and interaction decisions are this section's own; rules decisions are never this section's to make — any disagreement between what the platform renders and what the kernel computes is resolved in the kernel's favor, always, per the kernel's own constitution.
- **Runtime authority:** the Learn face holds no credentials and no persistent state. The Play face, once admitted, is the only holder of the Cloudflare Durable Object and D1 credentials the plan provisions for it; it must not delegate that authority to a client.
- **Section health:** per Clause 2.3, this section's health is computed from its declared incidence (cover, overlaps, restrictions above), not asserted by fiat — once both members are admitted and materialized, a conformance pass computes whether the declared overlap actually holds (zero disagreement) or must be reported with a quantified refusal, rather than assumed.

## Non-ownership

`weiqi-platform` does not own: rules logic of any kind (legality, scoring, ko/superko, SGF, semantic-event recognition — all `weiqi-kernel`'s, consumed read-only); corpus authorship (lessons, glossary terms, rulesets prose remain `weiqi-services-section`'s own `content/`, authored there and only rendered here); bot/engine hosting (GnuGo, KataGo, and the bare-metal analysis box are explicitly out of this section's boundary per the plan, reserved for a later, separately-constituted capacity); and billing/monetization (Stripe is provisioned infrastructure the plan explicitly defers, "out of scope until the platform has users" — this section does not admit a billing face by implication of that provisioning existing).

## Refusal conditions

- The Learn face must refuse to open a network connection, hold a key, or read a clock it was not handed by its own render call — any such need is evidence the responsibility belongs to the Play face, not a reason to compromise the Learn face's purity.
- Neither face may reimplement or shadow kernel logic (legality, scoring, event recognition) locally "for speed" or convenience; any move validation not delegated to `weiqi-kernel` is a refusal-worthy violation of the declared overlap restriction.
- The Play face (once admitted) must refuse a client-submitted move that the kernel rejects, with no override path, and must refuse to broadcast game state it cannot attribute to a kernel-validated position.
- This section must refuse to admit the Play face into its cover until Phase 1 has shipped and the board has separately authorized Phase 2, per the plan's roadmap and the board challenge's acceptance test 4 ("refuse materialization without explicit authority").
- This section must refuse to let the two faces' board-rendering or event-naming logic diverge, per the declared restriction above; a detected divergence is a defect in the section's health, not a matter of local team preference.

## Board authorization

The 561 Group board approved the Weiqi Platform Plan (`content/text/documents/articles/notes/weiqi-platform-plan.md`, dated 2026-08-18) on 2026-08-18, including its "Board decisions requested" item 1: "Approve platform placement inside `weiqi-services-section` and the two child-section constitutions (kernel, platform app)," and item 5, "Confirm education-first sequencing (Phase 1 ships before any multiplayer)," which this record's cover directly encodes (Learn admitted now, Play declared but withheld). This record discharges that authorization's platform half. It authorizes the *constitution* of the section and its declared cover — it does not authorize materialization of any filesystem, package, or protocol projection for either member, and it specifically does not authorize admitting the Play face's own constitution yet; that remains gated on the board's Phase 2 decision.

## Open obligations

- **Naming form**, as with the kernel: `weiqi-platform` (bare, per the plan and the instructing task) vs. `weiqi-platform-services-section` (per corpus-wide convention for a covered section). Not settled here.
- **The Learn service's own constitution record is still owed.** This document constitutes the section; it is not a substitute for `weiqi-platform-learn-service`'s own record (purpose/inputs/outputs/customers/authority/non-ownership/refusal conditions at the service level, generative parent = this section). That record — and only after it exists — is what licenses a `services/weiqi-platform/…` (or `apps/…`) directory to appear for the Learn face, per the plan's "no speculative scaffolding" rule.
- **The Play service is intentionally unconstituted.** Its cover entry above is a declared placeholder, not an admission; no constitution record should be written for it before the board's Phase 2 authorization, per the plan's own gating and the board challenge's acceptance test 4.
- **Board decisions requested items 2–4** of the plan (domain choice, Cloudflare-first confirmation, public-license posture) are outside this constitution's scope; they affect materialization, not the section's admission, and remain open per the plan.
- **Restricted-Yoneda leg agreement** (2026-08-11 derivation, Clause 1.2/PPA-FR-040) applies here as it does to the kernel: this section's identification of its own future apex, manifest, and protocol legs is a checked runtime condition once those legs exist, not an assumed fact now.
- **2026-08-19: sibling kernel materialization resolved, this section's own naming still open.** The [Weiqi Kernel Constitution](./weiqi-kernel-constitution.md)'s naming-form obligation is now settled — the kernel is materialized at `apps/weiqi-kernel` (bare name, no `-service` suffix), because the board's product-spine derivation places pure, no-network packages under `apps/`, not `services/`. That resolution is specific to the kernel's singular-service form; it does not resolve this section's own naming-form obligation above (`weiqi-platform` vs. `weiqi-platform-services-section`), since a covered section with a future keyed/socketed Play face is not the pure-package shape the same derivation clause addresses. The kernel's test suite state is recorded in its own README (`apps/weiqi-kernel/README.md`).

## What comes next

The Learn face's own constitution record is the next act this section owes itself before any code, README, or package.json may appear under its cover. See the sibling [Weiqi Kernel Constitution](./weiqi-kernel-constitution.md) for the service both faces of this section will depend on and must never reimplement.

rooms.description: Audience: the 561 Group board and future implementing agents. A full-spectrum plan for building the richest weiqi web gaming platform this repository's research supports, with new-player education as the organizing principle.
rooms.body:
# Weiqi Platform Plan

## Thesis

Every major Go server treats playing and learning as separate products: you play on OGS or Fox, you learn on GoMagic or BadukPop or a book. This repository's weiqi corpus — a dependency-linked glossary, a sequenced lesson curriculum with a uniform worked-example/exercise template, and a formal OWL/SHACL ontology binding it together — is precisely the asset that lets us fuse them. The platform's differentiator is **glossary-linked play**: the rules engine recognizes the concepts the corpus defines (atari, ko, capture, connection, eye, life-and-death) as they occur on the board, and the interface surfaces the corpus's own definitions and lessons at the moment they become relevant. The game explains itself while you play it. No incumbent does this, and no incumbent has the content architecture to do it.

The build motto, consistent with house doctrine: the engine is the executable form of the glossary. Each glossary term corresponds to a named predicate or event in the rules kernel, documented in both directions. Code is a perfect model of the theory, not merely working.

## What we already have

**Content.** Four sequenced weiqi lessons (overview → living groups and eyes → komi and handicap, with history as a parallel entry), ten dependency-linked glossary terms in three natural clusters (tactical: liberty–atari–capture–ko; scoring: territory–komi–handicap; structural: connection–eye–life-and-death), parent board-games and games curricula that position weiqi genealogically, and an eight-lesson ludics (theory of play) curriculum giving us an unusually principled design vocabulary (magic circle, paidia↔ludus, agon/alea, flow, Sutton-Smith's rhetorics).

**Schema.** The Ludic ASR ontology (OWL + SHACL) with typed content classes (term, lesson, specification, text, topic) and relations (defines, requires, teaches, uses-mechanic, cites) — a machine-checkable concept graph the product can consume directly as a skill tree and hover-card API.

**Infrastructure.** A provisioned Cloudflare account (Workers, D1, R2, Workers AI, DNS-edit tokens), a proven wrangler-via-GitHub-Actions deploy pattern (561.group), a second precedented deploy pattern (Node + systemd + Caddy on the box), in-house packages on a local Verdaccio registry (`@red-cup-engineering/http-server`, `organizing-with-the-semantic-web`, `561-group-website-theme`), and Stripe keys should monetization ever matter.

**Governance.** The service-section constitution and corpus-normalization/move-content skills, which tell us exactly where and how the platform's parts should live.

## What we do not have

- **No game code anywhere.** No engine, board renderer, SGF handling, or server. The platform is a greenfield build; only infrastructure and content are reusable.
- **An incomplete ruleset.** The corpus covers simple ko but not superko, suicide, seki, area-vs-territory scoring, pass/end-of-game procedure, dead-stone settlement, handicap placement conventions, or standard komi values. These must be authored as content *and* encoded in the kernel.
- **No strategy or training material.** No joseki, fuseki, tesuji, yose, tsumego, rank-system explainer, or annotated games; no SGF records at all.
- **Corpus hygiene debt.** A 174-file ludics triage inbox mixing stale weiqi duplicates with unrelated material, four inconsistent provenance conventions, missing index/landing pages and dead relative links, a missing README/package.json on the game-science ludics section, and a name collision between two `ludics-services-section` packages (play-theory vs Girard proof-theory).

## Product vision: three faces, one graph

1. **Play** — real-time and correspondence games, bots, clocks, ratings, handicap.
2. **Learn** — an interactive curriculum from first stone to single-digit kyu, built from the corpus's lesson template.
3. **Read** — the living glossary and library, served both as pages and as an API the other two faces consume.

All three faces are views over one concept graph (the ASR ontology). A capture in a live game, an exercise in a lesson, and the glossary entry for "capture" are the same node seen three ways.

## Pedagogy: the education architecture

This is the platform's center of gravity, so it gets the most detailed treatment.

**The onboarding ladder** follows proven Go pedagogy and happens to match the corpus's own dependency ordering:

1. *Capture Go* (atari-go) on 7×7/9×9 — only liberties and capture, the corpus's overview lesson made playable. First session, no account required.
2. *Full rules on 9×9* — territory, ko, passing, scoring introduced one game at a time.
3. *13×13* — opening direction, bigger groups, first joseki-shaped ideas.
4. *19×19* — the full game, introduced only when the player chooses it.

**Lessons become interactive.** The house lesson template (Audience → Learning goal → Worked example → Exercises with collapsible answers → What comes next) ports one-to-one onto an interactive board widget: worked examples become step-through board sequences; exercises become playable problems whose "answer" reveal is a replay with commentary. The four existing lessons are the pilot conversions; the template then scales to every new lesson we author.

**The concept graph is the skill tree.** The ontology's `requires`/`teaches`/`defines` relations give us mastery tracking for free: a player's profile records which concepts they have been taught, exercised, and demonstrated in live play (the kernel's semantic events provide the evidence — "you escaped atari correctly 9 of 11 times this week"). Progression, review scheduling (spaced repetition over tsumego), and lesson recommendations all read from this graph rather than an ad-hoc XP system.

**Glossary-linked play, concretely.** During and after games, the kernel annotates moves with recognized events: atari given/escaped, capture, ko started/resolved, group connected/cut, eye formed/falsified, group settled/killed. Beginners get gentle real-time surfacing ("this group is in atari" with a hover-card from the glossary); everyone gets a post-game timeline of concept events; teachers get them as anchors for review comments. The annotation vocabulary *is* the glossary — every event links to its term page.

**Ludics-informed design decisions**, using our own theory corpus:

- *Paidia → ludus gradient*: the platform's spaces run from free sandbox (analysis board, no stakes) through casual and teaching games to ranked play; the UI makes the register of each space explicit, echoing the magic-circle lesson.
- *Ritual marks the circle*: game start (nigiri), resignation, and post-game review are given deliberate ceremony in the UI — small, but it teaches Go culture as part of the game, the way the RPG corpus treats table culture.
- *Flow*: bot ladder and matchmaking target the flow channel — adaptive opponent strength keeps challenge slightly above skill; the Sutton-Smith rhetorics remind us to support play-as-identity (profiles, journals) and play-as-imaginary (named puzzles, storied classic games), not only play-as-progress (ratings).

**Content to author** (the education backlog, roughly in order): rules-completeness suite (superko variants, suicide, seki, area vs territory scoring, end-of-game procedure, handicap/komi tables by ruleset); a graded tsumego collection (life-and-death first, then tesuji) with SGF sources; "how ranks work" (kyu/dan, rating-to-handicap mapping — operationalizing the komi-and-handicap lesson); opening principles and first joseki on 9×9/13×13; annotated classic and instructive games; etiquette and culture guide. Each item lands as ontology-conformant markdown so the platform ingests it like the existing corpus.

**Teaching humans, not just content**: teaching-game mode (free branch exploration inline, teacher stones, shared pointer), a mentor ladder pairing single-digit kyu players with beginners, and beginner-protected rooms. The tabletop-RPG section's table-culture and safety-tool material is the in-house model for how to write the community norms.

## The rules kernel

A pure, dependency-free TypeScript package — working name `@lenticule-science/weiqi-kernel`, final name subject to the constitution step.

- Immutable position representation; Zobrist hashing; pluggable superko regimes (simple ko, positional/situational superko) and rulesets (Chinese, Japanese, AGA, New Zealand, Ing) as declared rule objects, not code forks.
- Scoring: area and territory, dead-stone marking protocol, seki detection, komi/handicap parameterization.
- SGF parse/serialize as a first-class module (import for tsumego/game records, export for every game played).
- **Semantic event layer**: the annotator that recognizes glossary concepts in move sequences — the platform's signature feature lives in the kernel, not the UI.
- Property-based tests (round-trip SGF, ko/superko invariants, scoring cross-checks against known positions), plus a corpus of regression positions drawn from the rules-completeness documents so the doctrine and the code cite each other.
- Runs identically in Workers, Node, and the browser; published to Verdaccio.

## Platform architecture

**Recommendation: Cloudflare-first.** The account is fully provisioned, the deploy pattern is proven in-repo, and the shape fits:

- **Workers + static assets** — site shell, lesson pages, glossary (rendered from the corpus markdown).
- **Durable Objects** — one per live game: WebSocket hub for players/spectators, authoritative clock (absolute, Fischer, byo-yomi), move validation via the kernel, reconnection; DO alarms drive correspondence-game timers.
- **D1** — users, game index, ratings history, learning-progress (concept-graph state).
- **R2** — SGF archive, media, tsumego collections.
- **Workers AI** — light NLP duties (turning analysis JSON into glossary-linked prose), not engine inference.

The bare-metal Node + systemd + Caddy pattern remains precedented and is the right home for the one component Cloudflare cannot host: a KataGo analysis service (below). Phase 1 needs none of the stateful pieces and can ship as a static-assets Worker exactly like 561.group today.

## Engines and AI

- **Bot ladder for learners**: scripted weak bots first (random-legal, greedy-capture, simple-heuristic) — ideal for capture-go onboarding and trivially hostable in the client or a Worker; GnuGo (classically weak-but-instructive) server-side; KataGo with strength caps and human-style networks at the top.
- **Deep review**: KataGo on owned hardware behind Caddy as a job queue (Workers enqueue, the box analyzes, results land in R2/D1). Score/ownership heatmaps, win-rate deltas, and — the differentiator — mistakes *translated into concept language* by joining KataGo output with the kernel's semantic events ("this move left the corner group with one eye" rather than "-14.2%").
- **In-browser hints**: a small WASM engine or policy net for instant local feedback in lessons, kept deliberately weak and explainable.
- Licensing note: GnuGo is GPL (server-side use is fine; distributing a WASM build triggers source-provision duties), KataGo's license and network-weights terms to be verified before bundling; SGF is an open format.

## Interface

- **The board is the product's face**: a crisp SVG board component — themeable via the 561-group theme package, faithful at 9/13/19 with star points, last-move and annotation layers (territory, ownership heatmap, concept-event badges).
- Touch: tap-then-confirm placement with magnified preview; desktop: hover ghost stone; keyboard: full coordinate navigation.
- Accessibility as a requirement, not a retrofit: screen-reader move announcements ("Black D4; the white stone at C3 is now in atari"), textual game state on demand, no color-only signals in overlays, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected.
- The glossary hover-card is a single shared component used in lessons, game annotations, chat, and library pages — one graph, one card.

## Ratings, matchmaking, fairness

Glicko-2 with provisional-rating handling, mapped to kyu/dan for display; automatic handicap-and-komi from rating gap (the komi-and-handicap lesson, operationalized — and linked from the match screen). Matchmaking pools by board size with beginner protection. Standard server-health policies from day one of ranked play: escaper timeouts, sandbagging detection, report/moderation flow.

## Community and culture

Rooms (beginner-protected, teaching, open), teaching-game mode, a mentor ladder, clubs, and eventually tournaments (McMahon pairing is the natural fit) and rengo/pair go as the first variants. The code of conduct and etiquette guide are authored as corpus content in the RPG section's table-culture tradition — culture is curriculum here, not terms-of-service boilerplate.

## Knowledge architecture and content operations

Prerequisite hygiene, before the corpus becomes a product dependency:

1. Sweep the ludics triage inbox (174 files): delete the stale weiqi duplicates, relocate the unrelated material to its owning sections, keep genuine ludics fragments.
2. Consolidate the four provenance conventions (recovered-research dirs, `--archive-DATE` siblings, `--preexisting-glossary` siblings, inline imported-source blocks) into one declared policy.
3. Create the missing landing pages (`weiqi` start-here linking the four lessons and ten terms) and repair dead relative links.
4. Fix structural inconsistencies: missing README/package.json on game-science ludics, the two-ludics name collision, version mismatches.
5. Extend the ontology with the new content classes the platform needs: `ruleset`, `tsumego`, `game-record` (SGF-backed), `curriculum-stage` — then SHACL-validate in CI so content debt cannot silently accumulate again.

The publishing pipeline reuses the semantic-site pattern (markdown + frontmatter → rendered pages + JSON-LD, as the Hugo archive already demonstrated) with one addition: a build step that emits the concept graph as JSON for the client.

## Governance and placement

Per the service-section constitution, new sections need constituted authority, so the plan is to **materialize inside the existing `weiqi-services-section`** rather than invent parallel structure: the section gains `services/` children for the kernel and the platform app (each with a written constitution record: purpose, inputs/outputs, customers, boundary, refusal conditions), while all content stays under the section's `content/`. No speculative scaffolding — each child directory appears only when its first real artifact does. Board (user) authorization for these constitutions is an explicit gate in Phase 0.

## Deployment, operations, economics

Deploy via the proven wrangler + GitHub Actions pattern; DNS-edit token allows `weiqi.561.group` (or a dedicated domain — board decision). Cloudflare costs are near-zero at hobby scale and degrade gracefully (Workers paid plan, D1/R2 free tiers are generous); the KataGo box is the only real capacity cost and is deferred to Phase 3. Stripe exists if premium features (deep reviews, courses) ever warrant it — explicitly out of scope until the platform has users. Decide a public license for the content and kernel before any public launch; everything is currently UNLICENSED/private.

## Roadmap

Each phase ships something complete and usable on its own.

**Phase 0 — Foundation.** Corpus hygiene (the five-item list above); author the rules-completeness suite; write and ratify the section constitutions; resolve the experimental-site README/package.json deployment discrepancy so the deploy story is unambiguous.

**Phase 1 — Learn (the education-first MVP).** Rules kernel with semantic events; SVG board component; interactive tutorial through the capture-go ladder; the four lessons converted to interactive form; graded tsumego player; glossary with hover-cards. Entirely client-side + static assets — no accounts, no server state, deployable exactly like 561.group. A complete, excellent way to learn Go, shipped before any multiplayer complexity.

**Phase 2 — Play.** Durable Object game rooms with WebSockets and clocks; D1 accounts and game archive; SGF export; scripted bots and GnuGo; casual matchmaking; correspondence play.

**Phase 3 — Understand.** KataGo review service on the box; concept-language review synthesis; ratings, rated play, automatic handicap; learning-progress tracking over the concept graph.

**Phase 4 — Belong.** Teaching games and mentor ladder; rooms and clubs; tournaments (McMahon); rengo; the culture curriculum in full.

## Risks and mitigations

- *One-person-plus-agents capacity*: phases are sized to be independently shippable; Phase 1 has no operational burden at all.
- *Realtime complexity*: quarantined in Durable Objects behind the kernel's pure validation; correspondence mode is the fallback if live play slips.
- *Engine hosting cost*: deferred to Phase 3; browser-weak-bots and GnuGo carry Phases 1–2.
- *Corpus debt bleeding into product*: Phase 0 is a hard gate; SHACL validation in CI keeps it fixed.
- *Governance friction*: constitutions are written once, early, with board sign-off, rather than renegotiated per artifact.

## Board decisions requested

1. Approve platform placement inside `weiqi-services-section` and the two child-section constitutions (kernel, platform app).
2. Choose the domain (`weiqi.561.group` vs dedicated).
3. Confirm Cloudflare-first architecture with the bare-metal box reserved for engine analysis.
4. Set the public-license posture for kernel and content ahead of launch.
5. Confirm education-first sequencing (Phase 1 ships before any multiplayer).
